subject: zenGarden
pitch: A small Japanese garden diorama on a square base. A curved red wooden bridge over a koi pond with three orange and white koi, a stone lantern, a little pine tree with cloud-shaped foliage, a cherry tree in full pink blossom dropping petals, raked white gravel with a few mossy rocks, and stepping stones leading to the bridge.
reasoning:
I'm planning a diorama scene around a 1.2m square base, and realizing I need to set up a root joint first since parts without one will throw an error.

For the layout, I'm placing a pond near the center-back with a flattened blue water disc, surrounding it with a ring of small rim stones, and adding a gravel patch on the ground plane. I'm also working out an arched bridge spanning the pond, using a swept path with a box-shaped cross-section to form the deck.

Now I'm adding support posts along both sides of the bridge with a swept rail on top, gold-capped end posts, and a series of thin plank boxes angled to follow the bridge's slope.

I'm laying out stepping stones curving toward the bridge end using flattened hexagonal cylinders in gray, then placing a gravel patch on the left front with thin raised rake lines and a few mossy rocks made from scaled dodecahedrons with greenish caps.

Next I'm positioning a stone lantern at the back-left with a square base, cylindrical shaft, platform, glowing firebox windows, a rotated four-sided cone roof, and a spherical finial. Then I'm adding a curved-trunk pine at the back-right with tiered cloud-like foliage clusters, and working out placement for a cherry tree near the pond on the left side.

I'm now building the cherry tree with a leaning swept trunk, branch sweeps, and clusters of pink and white icosphere blossoms scattered across the canopy, plus around 40 small flat pink petals scattered falling onto the water, ground, and air using tiny thin cylinders. I'm also starting to place three koi swimming along curved paths in the pond.

Still writing koi colors and geometry...

Defining body path points and radius profile...

Still positioning the tail cone...

I'll simplify by skipping pectoral fins and just adding a small dorsal box and tiny eye spheres on the head to keep things modest. Now I'm setting up helper functions for boxes and parts, then placing the lantern pieces—a base, shaft, and other components—at the fish's side near the ground.

Continuing to position the lantern: the hexagonal platform sits atop the shaft, a gray firebox rests on the platform with crossing yellow emissive boxes poking through to suggest glowing windows, and a four-segment cone rotated 45° forms the roof on top.

Now I'm defining the finial (sphere plus small cone) at the very top, and sketching a mossy patch as a flattened green sphere on the base. For the pine tree, I'm laying out a curved trunk using sweep points with tapering radius, then planning foliage as clustered tiers to create a layered canopy look.

I'm placing several flattened sphere clusters at different heights and offsets to build the pine's foliage tiers, using two shades of dark green and adding small branch sticks beneath the lower tiers. Then I start setting up the cherry tree's trunk path at a different position on the ground.

Now I'm detailing the cherry tree: a curved brown trunk, a few branch rods extending toward the pond, and a canopy made of faceted icosahedron blossom blobs scattered in pink tones around the upper branches. I'm also starting to scatter falling and ground petals near the tree.

Still writing petal placement...

I'm finalizing the bridge and stepping stone positions so they connect smoothly near the pond center, then moving on to the base structure—a dark wood outer frame box topped with a slightly raised ground layer for the garden surface.

I'm skipping extra turf tufts and keeping it simple, placing a few scattered rocks on the gravel bed and adding rake lines between them, with a torus ring suggesting raked gravel circling the main rock.

Now I'm working through the component structure—default export, rotation handling in degrees, and setting up a sweep function for the bridge deck that defines a flat box cross-section following a path, using the tangent direction to derive consistent normal and binormal frames for the radius profile.

Next I'm adding rails as swept hexagonal tubes offset along the deck, posts as vertical boxes, and defining the deck's curved height profile with a parabolic function between the bridge ends, then placing individual plank boxes across the width with slight rotation and a lighter red-brown color, plus beginning the arch support structure underneath.

I'm now writing a koi fish function that rotates points by an angle and sweeps a curved body path with circular cross-sections to build the fish shape.

Adding eyes, dorsal fin, and pectoral fins...
